clues: A town in the south of Spain lies in a rich, green valley. Small streams cross it, and the high hills of a tall range rise close by.
The sea and the hills wrap round this town and make a small climate of its own. The sun shines here on more than three hundred days each year.
In the first years of the nineteen nineties, Walt Disney first picked this town for its big new park in Europe. Paris won the park in the end.
Its beaches stretch along the coast for twenty-one kilometres of sand. That long, bright shore is why so many guests come here for a beach break.
Its heart is a white-walled old town full of small shops and pretty squares. Guests love to come here at all times of the year.
